label: October 2026
desc: Starter: polite phrases and friendly everyday words.
Everyday formal verbs and casual chat.
Formal email language and relaxed British English.
Academic adjectives and common informal expressions.
Advanced formal words and business idioms.
Rare formal vocabulary and expressive idioms.

words.def: Certain to happen; impossible to avoid or prevent.
words.ex: Some disagreement is inevitable when ten people work on one project.
words.ex2: With so many cars on one road, traffic jams are inevitable every morning.
words.watch: Use 'it is inevitable that + clause', not 'it is inevitable to + verb'.
words.prompt: Say something that will certainly happen in your town or your life in the next ten years, and why.
words.model: It is inevitable that the city will get more crowded, because thousands of students move here every year.
qs: What is one inevitable part of starting a new job or school?
Which changes in technology do you think are inevitable in the next twenty years?

up.plain: Mistakes are certain to happen when you learn something new.
up.model: Mistakes are inevitable when you learn something new.

pl: Taki, który na pewno się wydarzy; nie da się go uniknąć.
ro: Sigur că se va întâmpla; nu poate fi evitat.

words.def: Existing as a natural, permanent part of something, so it can't be removed.
words.ex: There is an inherent risk in every kind of investment.
words.ex2: Some stress is inherent in any important exam.
words.watch: The preposition is 'inherent in': 'the risks inherent in the job', not 'inherent of'.
words.prompt: Name a risk or problem that is a natural part of a job, sport or hobby.
words.model: Being tired all the time seems to be inherent in working night shifts.
qs: What risk is a natural part of a job you know well?
Is there a weakness inherent in social media? What is it?

up.plain: Danger is a natural part of mountain climbing.
up.model: Danger is inherent in mountain climbing.

ro: Care face parte, în mod natural și permanent, din ceva.

words.def: Decided by someone's personal choice or by chance, with no clear reason or rule behind it.
words.ex: The deadline felt arbitrary; nobody could explain why it had to be Friday.
words.ex2: The teacher's seating plan seemed arbitrary to the students.
words.watch: Arbitrary is stronger than 'random'. It suggests one person decided, and had no good reason.
words.prompt: Describe a rule at school, at work or in a game that seems to have no good reason behind it.
words.model: Our office has an arbitrary rule that nobody can book a meeting room for more than one hour.
qs: Have you ever been given a grade or a decision that felt arbitrary? What happened?
Which rule in your country seems arbitrary to you?

up.plain: The manager chose the date for no reason at all.
up.model: The manager chose an arbitrary date.

pl: Ustalony według czyjegoś widzimisię lub przypadkiem, bez jasnego powodu.
ro: Decis după bunul plac al cuiva sau la întâmplare, fără un motiv clar.

words.def: Seeming reasonable or probably true, although you can't be certain.
words.ex: His excuse sounded plausible until we checked the train times.
words.ex2: It is plausible that the meeting will move to Thursday.
words.watch: Plausible means something seems true, not that it is true. If you are certain, say 'true' or 'proven'.
words.prompt: Think of a story or an excuse that sounded believable at first. What was it?
words.model: He gave a plausible excuse for missing the lesson, but it turned out that he had overslept.
qs: What is a plausible reason for a friend to cancel plans at the last minute?
Which prediction about the future do you find plausible?

up.plain: Her reason for being late sounded believable.
up.model: Her reason for being late sounded plausible.

pl: Brzmiący rozsądnie i prawdopodobnie prawdziwy, choć nie ma pewności.
ro: Care pare rezonabil sau probabil adevărat, deși nu e sigur.

words.def: Clear, well organised and logically connected, so it is easy to follow.
words.ex: Her essay was coherent: every paragraph led naturally to the next.
words.ex2: After a long night, he could hardly give a coherent answer.
words.watch: Coherent is about how ideas hold together. For one easy sentence, say 'clear' instead.
words.prompt: Describe a lesson, talk or film that was easy (or hard) to follow, and say why.
words.model: The lecture was coherent because the speaker linked every example back to one main idea.
qs: What makes a presentation coherent?
Think of a film whose story wasn't coherent. What went wrong?

up.plain: His talk was clear and easy to follow.
up.model: His talk was coherent and easy to follow.

pl: Jasny, dobrze uporządkowany i logicznie połączony.
ro: Clar, bine organizat și legat logic.

words.def: Common or widespread in a particular place, time or group of people.
words.ex: Smartphones became prevalent in classrooms within a few years.
words.ex2: Back pain is prevalent among people who sit all day.
words.watch: Prevalent describes how common something is in a group, so it usually goes with 'among' or 'in'.
words.prompt: Name a habit, app or problem that has become common among people your age.
words.model: Short video apps have become prevalent among my students over the last two years.
qs: Which habit is prevalent among people in your country?
What kind of job is becoming more prevalent among young people?

up.plain: This habit is very common among teenagers.
up.model: This habit is prevalent among teenagers.

pl: Częsty w danym miejscu, czasie lub grupie ludzi.
ro: Frecvent într-un anumit loc, timp sau grup de oameni.

words.def: Easily harmed, hurt or attacked, either physically or emotionally.
words.ex: An old password leaves your account vulnerable to attack.
words.ex2: Young plants are vulnerable to frost in early spring.
words.watch: The preposition is 'vulnerable to something', not 'vulnerable for' or 'vulnerable of'.
words.prompt: Describe a person, place or system that needs extra protection, and say what the danger is.
words.model: Small shops are vulnerable to sudden rises in rent.
qs: Which people in your city are most vulnerable in winter?
How can you make your phone less vulnerable to hackers?

up.plain: Old computers can easily be attacked by viruses.
up.model: Old computers are vulnerable to viruses.

pl: Łatwy do skrzywdzenia lub zaatakowania, fizycznie lub emocjonalnie.
ro: Ușor de rănit sau de atacat, fizic sau emoțional.

words.def: Done on purpose, after thinking about it, rather than by accident.
words.ex: Leaving his name off the list was deliberate, not a mistake.
words.ex2: The company made a deliberate decision to keep prices low.
words.watch: The adjective ends /-rət/; the verb 'to deliberate' (discuss carefully) ends /-reɪt/.
words.prompt: Describe something you did on purpose that other people thought was an accident, or the opposite.
words.model: Her long pause was deliberate; she wanted everyone to think about the question.
qs: Describe a deliberate choice you made about your studies or career.
Have you ever made a mistake that someone thought was deliberate?

up.plain: She broke the glass on purpose.

pl: Zrobiony specjalnie, po zastanowieniu, a nie przez przypadek.
ro: Făcut intenționat, după ce te-ai gândit, nu din greșeală.
tr.ffpl: Uwaga: deliberate to „celowy”. Nie myl z „deliberować” (długo się naradzać), które po angielsku to deliberate jako czasownik, wymawiany inaczej.

words.def: Having more than one possible meaning, so it is not clear which one is intended.
words.ex: Her reply was ambiguous: 'maybe later' could mean yes or no.
words.ex2: The ending of the novel is deliberately ambiguous.
words.watch: Ambiguous means two or more meanings are possible. If something has no clear meaning at all, 'vague' is often the better word.
words.prompt: Describe a message, sign or instruction that could be understood in two ways.
words.model: The sign 'Fine for parking' is ambiguous: it could mean parking is allowed or that you will pay a fine.
qs: Have you ever received an ambiguous text message? What did it say?
Why do politicians sometimes give deliberately ambiguous answers?

up.plain: The message could mean two different things.

pl: Mający więcej niż jedno możliwe znaczenie.
ro: Care are mai multe sensuri posibile.

words.def: Possible to do or achieve in practice, with the time, money and people you have.
words.ex: With only two weeks left, a full redesign isn't feasible.
words.ex2: Is it feasible to finish the report before lunch?
words.watch: Feasible is about whether something can really be done, not whether it is likely. 'It's feasible that it will rain' is wrong; say 'it's possible that …'.
words.prompt: Describe a plan or idea you had, and say whether it was feasible and why.
words.model: Cycling to work is feasible for me because I live only four kilometres from the office.
qs: Is it feasible for you to learn a new language in one year? Why or why not?
What is one change that would be feasible for your school or company to make?

up.plain: Finishing the project by Friday is possible in practice.
up.model: Finishing the project by Friday is feasible.

pl: Możliwy do zrobienia w praktyce, przy czasie, pieniądzach i ludziach, którymi dysponujesz.
ro: Posibil de făcut în practică, cu timpul, banii și oamenii pe care îi ai.

words.def: Not wanting to do something, so you do it slowly or only because you have to.
words.ex: Many people are reluctant to change their passwords.
words.ex2: She was reluctant to leave her old team.
words.watch: Use 'reluctant to + base verb': 'reluctant to speak', not 'reluctant for speaking' or 'reluctant of'.
words.prompt: Talk about something you were reluctant to do at first but are glad you did.
words.model: I was reluctant to join the gym at first, but now I go three times a week.
qs: What were you reluctant to do as a child?
Why are some people reluctant to use online banking?

up.plain: He didn't really want to lend me his car.
up.model: He was reluctant to lend me his car.

pl: Taki, który nie chce czegoś robić i robi to powoli albo z musu.
ro: Care nu vrea să facă ceva și îl face încet sau doar pentru că trebuie.

words.def: A polite greeting you use before about 12 o'clock.
words.ex: Good morning, Mrs Smith. How are you today?
words.ex2: The teacher said good morning to the class.
words.watch: Use good morning to say hello, not goodbye. To say goodbye at night, say good night.
words.prompt: How do you greet your teacher or your boss when you arrive in the morning?
words.model: I say good morning to my boss when I arrive at work.
qs: Who do you say good morning to every day?
What time do you stop saying good morning?

pl: Grzeczne powitanie używane mniej więcej do godziny 12.
ro: Salut politicos folosit până pe la ora 12.

words.def: A polite way to show you are happy that someone helped you or gave you something.
words.ex: Thank you for your email, Mr Jones.
words.ex2: Thank you very much for your help.
words.watch: Thank you is two words. Thankyou as one word is a spelling mistake.
words.prompt: Write one polite sentence to thank someone who helped you this week.
words.model: Thank you for helping me with my homework yesterday.
qs: How do you thank a shop assistant in English?
Who was the last person you said thank you to?

pl: Grzeczny sposób, by okazać wdzięczność za pomoc lub prezent.
ro: Mod politicos de a arăta că ești recunoscător pentru ajutor sau pentru ceva primit.

words.def: A polite phrase to get someone's attention or to ask them to move.
coll: excuse me, where is the station?
words.ex: Excuse me, where is the train station?
words.ex2: Excuse me, can I sit here?
words.watch: Say excuse me before you interrupt or ask a stranger something. Say sorry after you make a mistake.
words.prompt: You are lost in a new city. What do you say to a stranger?
words.model: Excuse me, can you tell me where the museum is?
qs: When do you say excuse me on a bus or a train?
How do you get a waiter's attention politely?

up.model: Excuse me, where is the bank?

pl: Grzeczny zwrot, by zwrócić czyjąś uwagę albo poprosić, żeby ktoś się przesunął.
ro: Expresie politicoasă pentru a atrage atenția cuiva sau a-l ruga să se mute.

words.def: A polite way to say what you want.
coll: I would like to book a room
words.ex: I would like a table for two, please.
words.ex2: I would like to book a room for Friday.
words.watch: After would like, use a noun or to + verb: I would like to book a room, not I would like book a room.
words.prompt: You are in a café. Order your favourite drink politely.
words.model: I would like a large cappuccino, please.
qs: What would you like to do this weekend?
Where would you like to travel next year?

up.model: I would like a coffee, please.

pl: Grzeczny sposób, by powiedzieć, czego chcesz.
ro: Mod politicos de a spune ce vrei.

words.def: A small word you add to make a request polite.
words.ex: Could you open the window, please?
words.ex2: Please sit down and wait.
words.watch: Put please at the start or the end of a request: Please close the door, or Close the door, please.
words.prompt: Ask a classmate for something you need, politely.
words.model: Could you lend me a pen, please?
qs: How many times do you say please in a normal day?
Is it rude to forget please in your language?

up.model: Could you give me the menu, please?

pl: Krótkie słowo, które sprawia, że prośba brzmi grzecznie.
ro: Un cuvânt mic care face o cerere politicoasă.

words.def: What you say when you leave someone or end a phone call.
words.ex: Goodbye, and thank you for coming.
words.ex2: We said goodbye at the airport.
words.watch: Goodbye sounds a little formal with friends. With friends, bye or see you is more natural.
words.prompt: How do you end a phone call with your doctor or your boss?
words.model: Thank you for your help. Goodbye.
qs: Who did you say goodbye to today?
Is it hard for you to say goodbye at airports?

up.model: Goodbye, and have a nice day.

pl: To, co mówisz, gdy się z kimś żegnasz lub kończysz rozmowę telefoniczną.
ro: Ce spui când pleci sau închei o convorbire telefonică.

words.def: A short, friendly way to say hello.
words.ex: Hi, Tom! How are you?
words.ex2: Say hi to your sister for me.
words.watch: Hi is for friends, family and classmates. In a job interview or an email to a stranger, use hello or good morning.
words.prompt: Write a short message to a friend you haven't seen for a week.
words.model: Hi Anna! How was your week?
qs: Who do you say hi to every day?
Do you say hi to your teacher, or something more formal?

pl: Krótki, przyjazny sposób, by się przywitać.
ro: Un mod scurt și prietenos de a saluta.

words.def: An informal way to say thank you.
words.ex: Thanks for the pizza!
words.ex2: Thanks a lot, see you tomorrow.
words.watch: Thanks is always plural: thanks, not thank. Thank needs you: thank you.
words.prompt: Your friend sent you a funny video. Reply with one short message.
words.model: Thanks for the video, it was so funny!
qs: What is the last thing you said thanks for?
Do you say thanks to bus drivers in your town?

ro: Mod informal de a spune mulțumesc.

words.def: An informal way to say yes.
family: yeah, right (when you don't believe something)
words.ex: Yeah, I can come to the party.
words.ex2: Are you hungry? Yeah, a bit.
words.watch: Yeah is fine when you speak with friends. In a formal email or an exam essay, write yes.
words.prompt: Your friend asks if you want to watch a film tonight. Answer informally.
words.model: Yeah, sure! What time does it start?
qs: Do you say yeah or yes more often?
When is yeah not polite enough?

ro: Mod informal de a spune da.

words.def: A short, friendly way to say goodbye.
words.ex: Bye! See you tomorrow.
words.ex2: She said bye and got on the bus.
words.watch: Bye is for friends and family. To a customer or in a formal email, use goodbye or kind regards.
words.prompt: End a phone call with your best friend.
words.model: OK, bye! Talk to you later.
qs: How do you say bye in your language when you're in a hurry?
Do you say bye or goodbye to your teacher?

pl: Krótki, przyjazny sposób, by się pożegnać.
ro: Un mod scurt și prietenos de a-ți lua rămas-bun.

words.def: Very good, fashionable or great.
words.ex: Your new phone is really cool.
words.ex2: That's a cool idea! Let's do it.
words.watch: Cool also means a bit cold: a cool evening. The informal meaning is 'great'.
words.prompt: Tell a friend about something cool you saw this week.
words.model: I saw a really cool bike in town yesterday.
qs: What is the coolest place in your town?
Which app do you think is really cool right now?

ro: Foarte bun, la modă sau grozav.

words.def: An informal way to say yes, all right or fine.
coll: is it OK if I sit here?
words.ex: OK, let's meet at six.
words.ex2: Is it OK if I open the window?
words.watch: OK and okay are both correct. In formal writing, use all right, acceptable or I agree.
words.prompt: Your friend wants to change the meeting time. Agree informally.
words.model: OK, no problem. Let's meet at seven.
qs: What do you do when you're not feeling OK?
Is OK a word in your language too?

up.plain: I agree with the new time.
up.model: OK, the new time is fine.

ro: Mod informal de a spune da sau în regulă.

words.def: To get something that someone gives or sends to you.
words.ex: I received your email this morning.
words.ex2: She will receive a prize for her work.
words.watch: Spelling: i before e except after c. Receive, not recieve.
words.prompt: Write one formal sentence about a letter or parcel you got.
words.model: I received a parcel from my aunt last week.
qs: What is the best present you have ever received?
How many emails do you receive in a day?

pl: Dostać coś, co ktoś ci daje lub wysyła.
ro: A obține ceva ce cineva îți dă sau îți trimite.

words.def: To answer someone, especially in writing.
words.ex: Please reply to this email by Friday.
words.ex2: I'm still waiting for a reply.
words.watch: We reply to someone or something: reply to my message, not reply my message.
words.prompt: Write the last line of a formal email asking for an answer.
words.model: Please reply to me as soon as possible.
qs: How quickly do you reply to messages?
Who never replies to your emails?

up.model: Please reply as soon as possible.

ro: A-i răspunde cuiva, mai ales în scris.

words.def: To tell someone facts, often in an official way.
words.ex: Please inform the teacher if you are ill.
words.ex2: We will inform you about the new timetable.
words.watch: Inform needs a person: inform someone of or about something. Information is uncountable: some information, not an information.
words.prompt: Write a formal sentence telling a manager you will be late.
words.model: I am writing to inform you that I will be late tomorrow.
qs: How does your school inform students about changes?
Who should you inform if you lose your passport?

up.plain: I'm telling you that the shop is closed.
up.model: We would like to inform you that the shop is closed.

ro: A-i comunica cuiva fapte, adesea în mod oficial.

words.def: To help someone, especially at work.
words.ex: How can I assist you today?
words.ex2: Two nurses assisted the doctor.
words.watch: Assist is more formal than help. Assistance is uncountable: some assistance, not assistances.
words.prompt: You work in a hotel. Greet a guest and offer help formally.
words.model: Good evening. How may I assist you?
qs: Who assists you most at school or work?
Have you ever assisted a tourist in your town?

ro: a ajuta, a asista pe cineva
A ajuta pe cineva, mai ales la muncă.
tr.ffro: Atenție: în engleză assist înseamnă „a ajuta”. „A asista la un eveniment” (a fi prezent, a urmări) se spune attend sau watch, nu assist.

words.def: To go to an event, a meeting or a school.
words.ex: All students must attend the meeting.
words.ex2: She attended a small school in the mountains.
words.watch: No to after attend: attend the meeting, not attend to the meeting. Attend to means deal with.
words.prompt: Write a formal sentence about an event you went to recently.
words.model: Last month I attended my cousin's wedding in Gdańsk.
qs: What was the last wedding or party you attended?
Is it important to attend every class?

pl: Iść na wydarzenie, spotkanie albo do szkoły.
ro: A merge la un eveniment, o ședință sau la școală.
tr.ffro: Atenție: attend nu înseamnă „a atenta” (a ataca). Attend a meeting = a participa la o ședință.

words.def: To ask for something politely or officially.
words.ex: I would like to request a new password.
words.ex2: We received your request yesterday.
words.watch: The verb has no for: request a room, not request for a room. The noun can take for: a request for help.
words.prompt: Write a formal sentence asking a school for some information.
words.model: I would like to request information about your evening courses.
qs: What was the last thing you requested from a company?
How do you request a day off at work or school?

up.plain: Can I have a new card?
up.model: I would like to request a new card.

pl: Poprosić o coś grzecznie lub oficjalnie.
ro: A cere ceva politicos sau oficial.

words.def: An informal word for a child.
words.ex: When I was a kid, I loved football.
words.ex2: The kid next door plays the drums.
words.watch: Kid as a verb means joke: Are you kidding? = Are you joking?
words.prompt: Tell a friend about something you loved when you were small.
words.model: When I was a kid, I played outside every day.
qs: What did you want to be when you were a kid?
Are kids today happier than kids in the past?

words.def: An informal word for a man. Guys can mean a group of any people.
words.ex: He's a really nice guy.
words.ex2: The guy in the shop was very helpful.
words.watch: Guys (plural) is often used for a mixed group of men and women: Hi guys! But a guy (singular) is a man.
words.prompt: Describe a nice person you met recently, informally.
words.model: I met a really friendly guy at the gym yesterday.
qs: Who is the funniest guy you know?
Do you say you guys when you talk to friends?

pl: Potoczne słowo na mężczyznę. Guys może oznaczać grupę dowolnych osób.
ro: Cuvânt informal pentru bărbat. Guys poate însemna un grup de oameni, de orice gen.

words.def: An informal word for things, when you don't need to name them.
words.ex: Can I leave my stuff here?
words.ex2: I've got loads of stuff to do today.
words.watch: Stuff is uncountable: a lot of stuff, not a lot of stuffs.
words.prompt: Tell a friend what's in your bag right now.
words.model: My bag is full of stuff: books, keys and snacks.
qs: Do you have too much stuff in your room?
What stuff do you always take on holiday?

up.plain: Please take your belongings with you.

pl: Potoczne słowo na rzeczy, gdy nie trzeba ich nazywać.
ro: Cuvânt informal pentru lucruri, când nu e nevoie să le numești.

words.def: Very good; great.
words.ex: We had an awesome time at the beach.
words.ex2: Your new haircut looks awesome!
words.watch: In older or formal English, awesome means 'very impressive and a little frightening'. In everyday speech it just means 'great'.
words.prompt: Tell a friend about an awesome day you had.
words.model: Last Saturday was awesome. We went kayaking on the river.
qs: What was the most awesome concert or match you've seen?
What awesome thing would you like to try?

words.def: To spend time with friends in a relaxed way.
words.ex: We often hang out at the shopping centre.
words.ex2: Do you want to hang out on Saturday?
words.watch: The past is hung out: Yesterday we hung out at the beach.
words.prompt: Tell a friend where you like to spend free time.
words.model: I usually hang out with my friends at the skate park.
qs: Where do young people hang out in your town?
Who do you hang out with most?

up.plain: I spend time with my friends.
up.model: I hang out with my friends.

pl: Spędzać czas z przyjaciółmi na luzie.
ro: a ieși cu prietenii, a pierde vremea
A petrece timp cu prietenii, relaxat.

words.def: To get or take something quickly, often food or drink.
words.ex: Let's grab a coffee after class.
words.ex2: I'll grab some sandwiches for lunch.
words.watch: Grab also means take something suddenly and roughly: He grabbed my arm. Double the b: grabbed.
words.prompt: Invite a friend for a quick drink or snack.
words.model: Do you want to grab a pizza after work?
qs: Where do you grab lunch on a busy day?
What do you grab before you leave the house?

up.plain: Shall we have a quick coffee?

pl: Szybko coś wziąć, często jedzenie lub picie.
ro: A lua ceva repede, adesea mâncare sau băutură.

words.def: To buy something; something you buy.
words.ex: Tickets can be purchased online.
words.ex2: Please keep your receipt as proof of purchase.
words.watch: Purchase sounds like 'per-chus', not like chase.
words.prompt: Write a formal sentence about something expensive you bought.
words.model: I purchased a new laptop last month.
qs: What was your best purchase this year?
Do you prefer to purchase things online or in shops?

ro: A cumpăra ceva; un lucru pe care îl cumperi.

words.def: To need something; to make something necessary.
words.ex: This job requires good English.
words.ex2: Passengers are required to show their passport.
words.watch: Be required to + verb is a formal way to say must: You are required to wear a helmet.
words.prompt: Write a formal sentence about what your job or course needs.
words.model: My course requires two hours of homework a day.
qs: What skills does your dream job require?
What documents are required to travel abroad?

pl: Potrzebować czegoś; sprawiać, że coś jest konieczne.
ro: A avea nevoie de ceva; a face ceva necesar.

words.def: To give someone something they need.
words.ex: The hotel provides free breakfast.
words.ex2: Please provide your full name and address.
words.watch: Provide someone with something, or provide something for someone. Not provide someone something.
words.prompt: Write a formal sentence about what your school or company gives people.
words.model: My company provides free coffee for all workers.
qs: What does your town provide for young people?
Which apps provide the best news?

up.model: We provide free Wi-Fi for all guests.

ro: A-i da cuiva ceva de care are nevoie.

words.def: Close to an exact number, but not exactly.
words.ex: The journey takes approximately two hours.
words.ex2: Approximately half of the students passed.
words.watch: Use about or around when you speak. Approximately sounds formal, like a report or an announcement.
words.prompt: Write a formal sentence about how long your journey to school or work takes.
words.model: My journey to work takes approximately forty minutes.
qs: Approximately how many people live in your town?
Approximately how many hours a week do you study English?

pl: Blisko dokładnej liczby, ale nie dokładnie.
ro: Aproape de un număr exact, dar nu exact.

words.def: About; on the subject of. Used in emails and letters.
words.ex: I am writing regarding your advertisement.
words.ex2: Do you have any questions regarding the course?
words.watch: Regarding often starts a formal email: Regarding your order, … Don't use it in a chat with friends.
words.prompt: Write the first line of a formal email about a job advert.
words.model: I am writing regarding the job advertised on your website.

pl: Bardzo dobry; przyjazne słowo, gdy się z czegoś cieszysz.
ro: Foarte bun; un cuvânt prietenos când te bucuri de ceva.

words.def: A friendly way to say that it is easy for you to help, or to answer thank you.
words.ex: Can you help me? No problem!
words.ex2: Thanks for the lift. No problem at all.
words.watch: With friends, no problem answers thank you. With a customer, you're welcome is more polite.
words.prompt: Your friend says thank you for your help. What do you say?
words.model: No problem! Call me if you need anything.
qs: What do you say when a friend asks for a small favour?
When is no problem not polite enough?

up.plain: You're welcome, it was a pleasure.

pl: Przyjazny sposób, by powiedzieć, że chętnie pomożesz, albo odpowiedzieć na „dzięki”.
ro: Un mod prietenos de a spune că ajuți cu plăcere sau de a răspunde la mulțumesc.

words.def: A friendly way to say hello or to ask a friend how they are.
words.ex: Hey Sam, what's up?
words.ex2: What's up? You look sad.
words.watch: Answer what's up with not much, not with I'm fine thank you.
words.prompt: Write the first message you send a friend in a chat.
words.model: Hey Leo, what's up? Do you want to play football later?
qs: How do you answer when a friend says what's up?
Who do you say what's up to?

pl: Przyjazne powitanie albo pytanie, co u kogoś słychać.
ro: ce faci?, ce mai e nou?
Un mod prietenos de a saluta sau de a întreba un prieten ce face.

words.def: To write to, phone or email someone.
words.ex: Please contact us if you have any questions.
words.ex2: You can contact me by email.
words.watch: Contact has no preposition: contact the hotel, not contact to the hotel.
words.prompt: Write the last line of a formal email asking someone to reply.
words.model: Please contact me if you need more information.
qs: How do you usually contact your teacher?
How can customers contact a shop?

up.plain: Text me if you need anything.
up.model: Please contact me if you need anything.

pl: Napisać, zadzwonić lub wysłać e-mail do kogoś.
ro: A scrie, a suna sau a trimite un e-mail cuiva.

words.def: To like one thing more than another.
words.ex: I prefer tea to coffee.
words.ex2: Would you prefer a window seat?
words.watch: Say prefer A to B: I prefer trains to buses. Not prefer A than B.
words.prompt: Do you prefer summer or winter? Give one reason.
words.model: I prefer summer to winter because I love swimming.
qs: Do you prefer books or films?
Would you prefer to work at home or in an office?

up.plain: I like tea more than coffee.

pl: Lubić jedną rzecz bardziej niż inną.
ro: A-ți plăcea un lucru mai mult decât altul.

words.def: To leave, especially at the start of a journey by train, bus or plane.
words.ex: The train departs from platform 4 at 9.15.
words.ex2: Our flight will depart on time.
words.watch: Depart is formal and used on tickets and timetables. In chat, say leave.
words.prompt: Write a short announcement for a bus or train.
words.model: The bus to Kraków will depart at 10 o'clock from stop B.
qs: What time does your bus or train usually depart?
Where do flights to London depart from in your city?

pl: Wyruszać, zwłaszcza pociągiem, autobusem lub samolotem.
ro: A pleca, mai ales la începutul unei călătorii cu trenul, autobuzul sau avionul.
tr.ffro: Atenție: depart înseamnă „a pleca”, nu „departe” (în engleză far).

words.def: To officially allow someone to do something.
words.ex: Smoking is not permitted in the hotel.
words.ex2: Students are not permitted to use phones in exams.
words.watch: Permit is common on signs. In conversation, say allow or let.
words.prompt: Write a sign for a library or a swimming pool.
words.model: Food and drink are not permitted in the library.
qs: What is not permitted in your school or office?
Are dogs permitted in shops in your country?

ro: A permite oficial cuiva să facă ceva.

words.def: A British informal word for television.
words.ex: There's nothing good on the telly tonight.
words.ex2: We watched telly all evening.
words.watch: Telly is British English. Americans say TV.
words.prompt: What did you watch on telly this week?
words.model: I watched a football match on the telly last night.
qs: How much telly do you watch?
What's your favourite thing on telly?

words.def: A British informal word for toilet.
words.ex: Sorry, where's the loo?
words.ex2: I need to go to the loo before we leave.
words.watch: Loo is friendly British English. In a restaurant you can also ask for the toilets.
words.prompt: You are at a friend's house. Ask where the toilet is.
words.model: Sorry, can I use your loo?
qs: How do you ask for the toilet politely in English?
Is loo British or American English?

up.plain: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

words.def: The spoken, informal way to say going to.
words.ex: I'm gonna call you later.
words.ex2: It's gonna rain this afternoon.
words.watch: Gonna is for speaking and texts only. Never write gonna in an essay or a formal email.
words.prompt: Text a friend about your plans for tonight.
words.model: I'm gonna watch the match at Tom's. Wanna come?
qs: What are you gonna do this weekend?
When should you not write gonna?

up.plain: I am going to call you later.

ro: o să (forma vorbită de la going to)
Forma vorbită, informală, pentru going to.

words.def: A strong, friendly way to say no, or to show you are very surprised.
words.ex: You won the lottery? No way!
words.ex2: There's no way I'm getting up at five.
words.watch: No way can mean surprise (Really?) or a strong no. Your voice shows which one.
words.prompt: A friend tells you surprising news. Reply in one line.
words.model: No way! You're moving to Australia?
qs: What news made you say no way recently?
What would you say no way to doing?

up.plain: I will definitely not do that.

pl: Mocne, przyjazne „nie” albo okrzyk dużego zaskoczenia.
ro: Un „nu” hotărât, sau o exclamație de mare surpriză.

words.def: Extra; more than was first planned or included.
words.ex: There is an additional charge for breakfast.
words.ex2: Please send any additional information by Friday.
words.watch: Additional comes before a noun: additional costs. In chat, extra is more natural.
words.prompt: Write a sentence for a hotel website about extra costs.
words.model: Parking is available at an additional cost of 20 złoty a night.
qs: Have you ever paid an additional charge you didn't expect?
What additional help would make learning English easier?

up.plain: There's an extra fee for bags.
up.model: There is an additional fee for luggage.

ro: În plus; mai mult decât s-a plănuit la început.

words.def: Enough for a particular purpose.
words.ex: Two hours should be sufficient time for the exam.
words.ex2: There was not sufficient evidence to prove it.
words.watch: Sufficient is formal. Don't write very sufficient: something is sufficient or it isn't.
words.prompt: Is one week's holiday sufficient? Give your opinion.
words.model: One week is not sufficient for me; I need at least two to relax.
qs: Do you get sufficient sleep during the week?
Is one hour a week sufficient to learn a language?

words.def: To begin, used in very formal or official language.
words.ex: The course will commence on 3 March.
words.ex2: Building work will commence next month.
words.watch: Commence sounds official. In everyday speech, say start or begin.
words.prompt: Write a formal notice about when an event starts.
words.model: The conference will commence at 9 a.m. in the main hall.
qs: When does the school year commence in your country?
What kind of documents use commence instead of start?

up.model: The meeting will commence at ten.

pl: Zaczynać; używane w bardzo formalnym lub urzędowym języku.
ro: A începe; folosit în limbaj foarte formal sau oficial.

words.def: To get something, especially by asking for it or working for it.
words.ex: You must obtain a visa before you travel.
words.ex2: Tickets can be obtained at the box office.
words.watch: Obtain is formal. In a chat with friends, say get.
words.prompt: Explain how to get a document or ticket in your country.
words.model: You can obtain a parking permit from the town hall.
qs: What documents did you need to obtain for a trip?
Where can you obtain information about courses?

up.plain: Where can I get a form?
up.model: Where can I obtain a form?

pl: Zdobyć coś, zwłaszcza prosząc o to albo pracując na to.
ro: A obține ceva, mai ales cerând sau muncind pentru asta.

words.def: A British informal word for very tired.
words.ex: I'm knackered after that run.
words.ex2: She was absolutely knackered after the night shift.
words.watch: Knackered is British and informal. At work, say exhausted or very tired.
words.prompt: Tell a friend why you're so tired today.
words.model: I'm knackered because I worked twelve hours yesterday.
qs: What makes you knackered?
How do you relax when you're knackered?

ro: Cuvânt britanic informal pentru foarte obosit.

words.def: A British informal word for a pound (£1).
words.ex: Can you lend me ten quid?
words.ex2: The tickets were only five quid each.
words.watch: Quid has no plural s: twenty quid, not twenty quids.
words.prompt: Tell a friend how much something cost you.
words.model: These trainers only cost me thirty quid in the sale.
qs: What can you buy for five quid?
What informal words for money do you know?

ro: Cuvânt britanic informal pentru o liră (1 £).

words.def: A British informal way to say thank you or goodbye, or what you say before you drink together.
words.ex: Cheers for the coffee, mate.
words.ex2: Cheers! Happy birthday!
words.watch: Cheers means thanks in British English. Don't use it in a formal email.
words.prompt: Thank a friend for something small in a text.
words.model: Cheers for the lift home last night!
qs: When do people say cheers in your country?
What else can cheers mean?

up.plain: Thank you very much for the lift.

pl: Brytyjskie potoczne „dzięki” lub „cześć”, a także toast.
ro: Mod britanic informal de a spune mulțumesc sau la revedere, și un toast.

words.def: To wait for a short time.
words.ex: Hang on, I'll get my coat.
words.ex2: Can you hang on a minute? I'm on the phone.
words.watch: Hang on is informal. In a formal call, say could you wait a moment, please?
words.prompt: A friend is waiting for you outside. Text them.
words.model: Hang on a sec, I'm just finding my keys.
qs: When do you ask someone to hang on?
What's a more formal way to say hang on?

words.def: Large in amount, size or importance.
words.ex: The company made a substantial profit last year.
words.ex2: Prices have risen substantially since 2020.
words.watch: Substantial is about size or amount, not about being solid. A substantial meal is a big one.
words.prompt: Describe a big change in your town, school or company.
words.model: There has been a substantial increase in the number of cyclists in my city.
qs: What would you do with a substantial amount of money?
What has changed substantially in your life recently?

pl: Duży pod względem ilości, rozmiaru lub znaczenia.
ro: Mare ca mărime, cantitate sau importanță.

words.def: Including everything or nearly everything that is needed.
words.ex: The guide gives a comprehensive list of museums in the city.
words.ex2: We need a comprehensive review of our safety rules.
words.watch: Comprehensive means complete. It doesn't mean easy to understand; that is comprehensible.
words.prompt: Recommend a book, website or course that covers a subject completely.
words.model: This website offers a comprehensive guide to English grammar.
qs: Where can you find comprehensive information about your city?
Is your phone insurance comprehensive?

up.plain: It's a full list of everything.

pl: Obejmujący wszystko lub prawie wszystko, co potrzebne.
ro: Care include tot sau aproape tot ce e necesar.

words.def: Happening after something else.
words.ex: The first meeting was difficult, but subsequent meetings went well.
words.ex2: He was subsequently offered a full-time job.
words.watch: Subsequent is formal. In speech, say later or after that.
words.prompt: Describe something that happened and what happened later.
words.model: I failed my first driving test, but I passed on the subsequent attempt.
qs: What did you learn in the first lesson that helped in subsequent ones?
What happened subsequently after you moved house?

up.model: He was subsequently offered a job.

words.def: Good enough or large enough for a need, but not excellent.
words.ex: The hotel room was adequate, but nothing special.
words.ex2: Many schools lack adequate funding.
words.watch: Adequate often sounds slightly negative: only good enough. Excellent is much stronger.
words.prompt: Describe a place or service that was OK but not great.
words.model: The food at the conference was adequate, but the coffee was terrible.
qs: Does your city have adequate public transport?
Is your home office adequate for working?

pl: Wystarczająco dobry lub duży na daną potrzebę, ale nie znakomity.
ro: Destul de bun sau de mare pentru o nevoie, dar nu excelent.
tr.ffpl: Uwaga: adequate to „wystarczający”, często z lekkim minusem. Polskie „adekwatny” (odpowiedni, trafny) to po angielsku zwykle appropriate.
tr.ffro: Atenție: adequate înseamnă mai ales „suficient, acceptabil”. „Adecvat” în sensul de potrivit se spune de obicei appropriate.

words.def: A decision that is very easy because the right choice is obvious.
words.ex: A free upgrade? That's a no-brainer.
words.ex2: Taking the job was a no-brainer.
words.watch: Write it with a hyphen: a no-brainer. It's too informal for an essay.
words.prompt: Describe a decision that was very easy for you.
words.model: Moving closer to work was a no-brainer: I saved two hours a day.
qs: What was a no-brainer decision for you this year?
Is learning English a no-brainer for your career?

pl: Decyzja bardzo łatwa, bo właściwy wybór jest oczywisty.
ro: O decizie foarte ușoară, pentru că alegerea corectă e evidentă.

words.def: To stop working on something, usually because you are tired or have done enough.
coll: decided to call it a day
time to call it a day
words.ex: It's eight o'clock. Let's call it a day.
words.ex2: After ten years, the band decided to call it a day.
words.watch: The verb changes: we called it a day yesterday.
words.prompt: Suggest stopping work to your colleagues.
words.model: We've done enough for today. Shall we call it a day?
qs: When do you usually call it a day at work or school?
When should a sports star call it a day?

pl: Przestać nad czymś pracować, zwykle ze zmęczenia albo dlatego, że zrobiło się dość.
ro: a încheia pe ziua de azi
A te opri din lucru, de obicei pentru că ești obosit sau ai făcut destul.

words.def: To do more than people expect of you.
coll: willing to go the extra mile
words.ex: Our teacher always goes the extra mile for her students.
words.ex2: The hotel staff went the extra mile to help us.
words.watch: The verb changes: she went the extra mile. Common in job interviews and reviews.
words.prompt: Describe a person who did more than you expected.
words.model: The waiter went the extra mile and brought my son a birthday cake.
qs: Who in your life always goes the extra mile?
When did you go the extra mile at work or school?

up.plain: She does more than she has to.
up.model: She always goes the extra mile.

Zrobić więcej, niż ludzie od ciebie oczekują.
ro: a face un efort în plus
A face mai mult decât se așteaptă oamenii de la tine.

words.def: To talk to someone briefly to share news or check how things are going.
words.ex: Let's touch base on Friday about the project.
words.ex2: I'm just touching base to see if you got my email.
words.watch: Touch base is common in office English, usually with with: touch base with the team.
words.prompt: Write a short message to a colleague suggesting a quick chat.
words.model: Can we touch base tomorrow morning about the budget?
qs: Who do you touch base with every week?
Is touch base used in your workplace?

pl: Krótko porozmawiać, żeby przekazać nowości lub sprawdzić, jak idzie.
ro: a lua legătura, a ne auzi
A vorbi pe scurt cu cineva pentru a da vești sau a verifica cum merg lucrurile.

words.def: Very careful about every small detail.
words.ex: She keeps meticulous records of every payment.
words.ex2: The trip was meticulously planned.
words.watch: Meticulous is positive. If someone is too careful, say pedantic or fussy.
words.prompt: Describe a person you know who pays great attention to detail.
words.model: My accountant is meticulous; she checks every receipt twice.
qs: In which jobs is meticulous work essential?
Are you meticulous when you write emails?

words.def: Causing harm or damage.
words.ex: Too much screen time can be detrimental to sleep.
words.ex2: The new road had a detrimental effect on local wildlife.
words.watch: Use detrimental to: detrimental to your health, not detrimental for.
words.prompt: Name a habit that harms people's health or work, and explain why.
words.model: Skipping breakfast can be detrimental to concentration at school.
qs: What habits are detrimental to your productivity?
Is social media detrimental to teenagers?

up.model: Smoking is detrimental to your health.

words.def: Not certain or final; done carefully because you are not sure.
words.ex: We have a tentative date for the meeting: 12 May.
words.ex2: The talks are tentatively scheduled for next week.
words.watch: A tentative plan may still change. A firm plan is fixed.
words.prompt: Describe a plan that is not fixed yet.
words.model: We've made tentative plans to visit Lisbon in the spring.
qs: What tentative plans do you have for next year?
When did you take tentative steps into something new?

pl: Niepewny lub nieostateczny; robiony ostrożnie, bo nie masz pewności.
ro: Nesigur sau nedefinitiv; făcut cu grijă pentru că nu ești sigur.

words.def: Most important or most noticeable.
words.ex: Let me summarise the salient points of the report.
words.ex2: The most salient feature of the design is its simplicity.
words.watch: Salient almost always goes with points, features or facts.
words.prompt: Summarise the main points of a news story you read.
words.model: The salient point of the article was that rents rose by 15 percent.
qs: What are the salient features of a good CV?
What is the most salient problem in your city?

ro: Cel mai important sau cel mai vizibil.

words.def: To change the rules or targets unfairly while someone is trying to achieve them.
words.ex: Every time we finish, the client moves the goalposts.
words.ex2: It's unfair to move the goalposts halfway through the project.
words.watch: The verb changes: they moved the goalposts. It is a complaint, so it sounds critical.
words.prompt: Describe a situation where the rules changed unfairly.
words.model: Our manager moved the goalposts by raising the sales target in the last week.
qs: Has anyone moved the goalposts on you?
Why do companies sometimes move the goalposts?

pl: Niesprawiedliwie zmieniać zasady lub cele, gdy ktoś próbuje je osiągnąć.
ro: A schimba pe nedrept regulile sau obiectivele în timp ce cineva încearcă să le atingă.

words.def: Back at the beginning because an attempt has failed.
words.ex: The deal fell through, so we're back to square one.
words.ex2: If the test fails, we'll go back to square one.
words.watch: Square one comes from board games. Use it when work is lost, not just started.
words.prompt: Describe a time a plan failed and you had to start again.
words.model: The computer crashed and I lost my essay, so I was back to square one.
qs: When were you last back to square one?
How do you stay positive when you're back to square one?

up.plain: We must start from the beginning again.

pl: Znowu na początku, bo próba się nie udała.
ro: Din nou la început, pentru că o încercare a eșuat.

words.def: To start an activity or process.
words.ex: Let's get the ball rolling with a quick introduction.
words.ex2: Her email got the ball rolling on the new project.
words.watch: Common at the start of meetings. Start the ball rolling means the same.
words.prompt: Open a meeting or a class in one sentence.
words.model: To get the ball rolling, could everyone share one goal for this month?
qs: How do you get the ball rolling in a new class?
What project would you like to get the ball rolling on?

ro: A începe o activitate sau un proces.

words.def: A situation where the rules are not clear, so it is hard to say what is right.
coll: a bit of a grey area
words.ex: Working from abroad is still a grey area in my contract.
words.ex2: Using AI for homework is a bit of a grey area.
words.watch: British spelling is grey; American is gray.
words.prompt: Describe a rule or situation that is not clearly right or wrong.
words.model: Downloading old films is a grey area in many countries.
qs: What is a grey area at your work or school?
Is sharing streaming passwords a grey area?

up.plain: The rules aren't clear about this.

pl: Sytuacja, w której zasady nie są jasne, więc trudno powiedzieć, co jest właściwe.
ro: O situație în care regulile nu sunt clare, așa că e greu de spus ce e corect.

words.def: Understood or enjoyed by only a small number of people with special knowledge.
words.ex: The lecture was too esoteric for most first-year students.
words.ex2: He has a rather esoteric interest in medieval maps.
words.watch: Esoteric can sound slightly critical: too specialised for ordinary people.
words.prompt: Describe a hobby or topic that only a few people understand.
words.model: My uncle collects esoteric facts about Polish railway history.
qs: Do you have any esoteric interests?
Why do some academic texts feel esoteric?

pl: Zrozumiały lub ciekawy tylko dla niewielu ludzi ze specjalną wiedzą.
ro: Înțeles sau apreciat doar de puțini oameni cu cunoștințe speciale.
tr.ffpl: Uwaga: esoteric to zwykle „hermetyczny, dla specjalistów”. Polskie „ezoteryczny” kojarzy się z magią i okultyzmem, a po angielsku to raczej occult lub mystical.
tr.ffro: Atenție: esoteric înseamnă de obicei „pentru specialiști, de nișă”, nu neapărat mistic sau ocult.

words.def: Having a harmful effect, especially slowly and in a way that is hard to notice.
words.ex: Misinformation has a pernicious effect on public trust.
words.ex2: The idea that girls are bad at maths is a pernicious myth.
words.watch: Pernicious suggests hidden, gradual harm. For sudden harm, say damaging or devastating.
words.prompt: Describe an idea or habit that slowly causes harm.
words.model: Constant comparison on social media has a pernicious effect on self-esteem.
qs: What pernicious myths exist about learning languages?
Is gambling advertising pernicious?

pl: Szkodliwy, zwłaszcza powoli i w trudny do zauważenia sposób.
ro: Dăunător, mai ales încet și greu de observat.

words.def: To make something deliberately unclear or difficult to understand.
words.ex: The report seems designed to obfuscate the real costs.
words.ex2: Politicians sometimes obfuscate rather than answer directly.
words.watch: Obfuscate implies intention. If something is unclear by accident, say confusing.
words.prompt: Describe a document or speech that hid the truth with complicated language.
words.model: The contract obfuscated the cancellation fees in tiny print.
qs: Why do companies obfuscate their terms and conditions?
How can you tell when someone is obfuscating?

up.plain: They made it confusing on purpose.

pl: Celowo sprawić, by coś było niejasne lub trudne do zrozumienia.
ro: A face ceva intenționat neclar sau greu de înțeles.

words.def: Done quickly and without real care or interest, only because it has to be done.
words.ex: He gave the report a perfunctory glance and signed it.
words.ex2: Her apology sounded perfunctory.
words.watch: Perfunctory describes actions, not people: a perfunctory check, not a perfunctory person.
words.prompt: Describe something someone did quickly without caring.
words.model: The doctor gave me a perfunctory examination and sent me home.
qs: Have you ever received a perfunctory apology?
Why are some job interviews perfunctory?

up.plain: He looked at it very quickly without caring.
up.model: He gave it a perfunctory glance.

pl: Zrobiony szybko i bez zaangażowania, tylko dlatego, że trzeba.
ro: Făcut repede, fără grijă sau interes, doar pentru că trebuie.

words.def: To accept something unpleasant that you can no longer avoid.
words.ex: I finally bit the bullet and booked the dentist.
words.ex2: We'll have to bite the bullet and raise prices.
words.watch: The past is bit: I bit the bullet yesterday.
words.prompt: Describe something unpleasant you finally decided to do.
words.model: I bit the bullet and told my boss I was leaving.
qs: What have you been putting off that you should bite the bullet on?
When did you last bite the bullet?

up.plain: I accepted it and did it.

pl: Zaakceptować coś nieprzyjemnego, czego nie da się już uniknąć.
ro: A accepta ceva neplăcut pe care nu-l mai poți evita.

words.def: Something that takes attention away from the real issue, sometimes on purpose.
coll: turn out to be a red herring
words.ex: The missing key was a red herring; the thief came through the window.
words.ex2: Talk of the budget is a red herring: the real problem is staff.
words.watch: Common in detective stories and debates.
words.prompt: Describe something in a film, book or debate that distracted from the real issue.
words.model: The butler in the film was a red herring; the real killer was the gardener.
qs: Can you think of a red herring in a crime story?
Why do debaters use red herrings?

up.plain: That's not the real issue; it's a distraction.

pl: Coś, co odciąga uwagę od prawdziwego problemu, czasem celowo.
ro: Ceva care distrage atenția de la problema reală, uneori intenționat.

words.def: To avoid saying something directly, usually because it is uncomfortable.
words.ex: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened.
words.ex2: She didn't beat around the bush: she said the plan wouldn't work.
words.watch: British English often says beat about the bush.
words.prompt: Ask someone to say something directly.
words.model: Don't beat around the bush; just tell me if I got the job.
qs: Do people in your culture beat around the bush?
When is it kinder to beat around the bush?

pl: Unikać mówienia czegoś wprost, zwykle bo to niezręczne.
ro: A evita să spui ceva direct, de obicei pentru că e incomod.

words.def: To talk about the most important thing immediately, without unnecessary details.
words.ex: Let's cut to the chase: how much will it cost?
words.ex2: I'll cut to the chase. We need more money.
